$comment: Glossary terms for the non-Copilot-Studio products: Microsoft Foundry, Agent Builder and declarative agents, the Microsoft 365 Copilot hub and Copilot controls, SharePoint AI, and AI Builder. Each definition follows Microsoft Learn.

foundry-project.plain: the workspace in Microsoft Foundry where a team builds with models and agents and shares access

hub-based-project.plain: an older kind of Foundry project that lives in a hub, which shares settings with every project inside it

foundry-playground.plain: a place in Foundry to try a model or an agent with your own prompts before you write any code

model-catalog.plain: the searchable list of models in Foundry that you can read about, compare, and deploy

token.plain: a small chunk of text, either a word or part of a word, that an AI model reads or writes

prompt-agent.plain: a Foundry agent you define with instructions, a model, and tools, which Foundry hosts and runs for you

hosted-agent.plain: a Foundry agent made from your own code, which Foundry runs for you

microsoft-copilot.plain: Microsoft's AI assistant for work in Microsoft 365 apps; Learn now uses this name for what was called Microsoft 365 Copilot

copilot-chat.plain: the chat experience for work in Microsoft Copilot, built into Microsoft 365 apps such as Teams and Outlook

copilot-controls.plain: a set of tools and settings that help an organization keep Copilot and agents safe, managed, and measured

agents-toolkit.plain: a set of developer tools for building agents and apps for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, and Office; it grew out of Teams Toolkit

billing-policy.plain: a record that links a group of users to an Azure subscription, so their Copilot use is billed there

azure-subscription.plain: an Azure account that services are created in and billed to

purview.plain: Microsoft's tools for protecting and governing data, such as audit logs and data loss prevention

restricted-content-discovery.plain: a SharePoint site setting that keeps its content out of organization-wide search and Copilot answers without changing who has access

dspm.plain: a Microsoft Purview view of where sensitive data is, who can reach it, and how well it is protected

soft-delete.plain: deleting something so it can still be brought back for a set time before it is removed for good

prebuilt-model.plain: an AI Builder model that is ready to use with no training, for jobs common to many businesses

custom-model.plain: an AI Builder model that you train on your own data so it fits your business

ai-hub.plain: the area of Power Apps and Power Automate where makers find AI Builder models and prompts

model-training.plain: the automatic step that teaches a model to solve your problem from your own data

prompt-builder.plain: the tool where makers write, test, and save prompts that apps, flows, and agents can reuse

document-processing.plain: AI that reads documents such as invoices and forms and saves the fields you care about

autofill-column.plain: a SharePoint library column that uses a plain-language prompt to fill itself in from each file

canvas-app.plain: a custom business app you build in Power Apps by dragging components onto a blank design surface, with no code

target-leakage.plain: when a training column gives away the answer, so a model looks great in training but fails on real data
